newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP confident of improved performance.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP confident of improved performance.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) on Friday said it was confident of an improved performance after reporting a 60.8 percent dive in annual net profit after abnormal items.
BHP managing director John Prescott said the A$976 million net abnormal loss shown in the accounts for the year ended May 31 would enable BHP to better capitalise on its strengths.
He said some assets written down might have no future with BHP and described the group as being in a transition phase.

"The company is moving from operating a particular set of assets, some of which are depleting, some of which are not going to have the same number of people working in them in future," he said in a tape-recorded interview released by BHP.
"Some of them are assets that perhaps we are not going to have in the future as we complete the review of our portfolio."
BHP earlier on Friday reported a dive in net annual profit after abnormals to A$410 million, but pre-abnormal earnings were in line with forecasts at A$1.386 billion, up seven percent.
Prescott said the abnormal losses, made up mostly of asset write-downs, were needed for BHP to go forward.
"We have sought to bring to account all the issues we have to deal with over the next two or three years that we think will affect our accounta," he said.
The write-downs involved its copper, minerals and petroleum assets. Its steel division also incurred restructuring charges.
